**Global Everbright Store Sdn. Bhd. – Quick Vetting Summary** | **Aspect** | **Key Points** | |------------|----------------| | **Company basics** | • **Name:** Global Everbright Store Sdn. Bhd. (formerly *Sinar Industries Sdn. Bhd.* – name change 25 Jun 2025)
• **Reg. No.:** SYN‑000267
• **Type:** Private limited company, active
• **Incorporated:** 28 Oct 1990
• **Location:** Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
• **Industry / Business:** Retail – textiles & *baju kurung* | | **Ownership & control** | • **Directors (3):** Managing Director (appointed 5 Jan 2024), Executive Director (since 1 Aug 2007), Independent Director (since 12 Dec 2008)
• **Shareholding:** 89.67 % held by Managing Director, 10.33 % by Executive Director – highly concentrated ownership | | **Financial health (FY 2022‑2024)** | • **Revenue growth:** RM 17.7 M → RM 19.4 M (≈ 10 % CAGR)
• **Profitability:** Gross margin 30‑33 %; net margin low (≈ 2‑3 %) – modest earnings after tax (RM 0.4‑0.5 M)
• **Liquidity:** Quick ratio 1.25‑1.49, cash‑to‑revenue improving to 15.7 % (2024)
• **Cash flow:** Operating cash flow positive each year, but free cash flow negative (CAPEX > OCF)
• **Leverage:** Debt‑to‑equity ≈ 0.76‑0.84; interest coverage 2.8‑3.3× – manageable but not strong | | **Operational efficiency** | • **Cash conversion cycle:** 69‑94 days (fluctuating)
• **Inventory turnover:** 4.4‑5.6× (reasonable for textile retail)
• **Asset turnover:** 0.86× (stable) | | **Legal exposure** | • **5 litigation cases (2023‑2025)** – all as plaintiff for breach of contract or debt recovery.
• **Outcomes:** 1 settled (RM 2.26 M claim), 1 pending (RM 0.18 M), 1 settled (RM 0.40 M), 1 dismissed, 1 withdrawn.
• **Potential risk:** Ongoing pending case (~RM 0.18 M) plus history of contract disputes. | | **Red flags / considerations** | • Highly concentrated ownership – limited board independence.
• Thin net profit margins; profitability relies on volume.
• Negative free cash flow suggests cash‑intensive growth or under‑performing CAPEX.
• Repeated breach‑of‑contract litigation may indicate supply‑chain or contractual management issues. | | **Why it might be worth a deeper look** | • Stable revenue growth in a niche retail segment (textiles & traditional wear).
• Strong liquidity (quick ratio > 1) and manageable leverage.
• Audited financials with unqualified opinions each year. | | **Why it might be passed** | • Low profitability and negative free cash flow could affect pricing or reliability as a partner.
• Concentrated ownership and recent legal disputes raise governance and risk concerns. | **Bottom line:** *Global Everbright Store* shows steady top‑line growth and solid liquidity, but thin margins, cash‑flow pressure, and a pattern of contract‑related litigation suggest a cautious approach. Recommend a deeper dive into contract management practices, cash‑flow forecasts, and governance structures before committing to a partnership.
